conviction_note: Small offsetting findings: the EPS bar ($0.50-0.51) sits at the low-middle of the company's own implied Q2 (~15% of a $3.25-3.75 FY = $0.49-0.56), the $71m of IEEPA tariffs outside the guide is the one large unpriced lever but management says it will reinvest most of it, and the July 24 Section 301 step-up to 12.5% on China/Vietnam is a guide headwind the July outlook did not assume. A crowded short (12.8% float, 9 days) and an -8.8% run-in point up; a name that fell on 6 of its last 7 prints, including a Q1 beat with raised sales guidance, points down. p_up 51 on an abs move of 15 gives +0.3. The findings sum to +0.8 because they are sized one by one and the reaction history is carried only in p_up.
bar: Q2 FY27 (Jun-Aug 2026) adj EPS $0.50 / revenue $443.2m (Benzinga preview, https://www.benzinga.com/node/61988956) and $0.51 / $441.45m with whisper $0.55 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HELE). Two sources agree within $0.01. Company-implied: CFO on the Q1 call said ~15% of FY adj EPS lands in Q2, which on $3.25-3.75 is $0.49-0.56 (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1888002-20260709). An outlier exists: Zacks Research's own Q2 estimate was $0.26 on 2026-07-29 with FY27 $2.85, below the company's FY guide (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/q2-eps-estimates-for-helen-of-troy-raised-by-zacks-research-2026-07-31/). Year-ago Q2 FY26 was adj EPS $0.59 on $431.8m.
positioning_check: Short interest 2,952,013 shares = 12.77% of float, 9.0 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-15, essentially flat vs prior (2,957,235) (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/HELE/short-interest, read 2026-10-07). That is crowded: a negative surprise is partly positioned for, and the squeeze is its own mechanism. Skew is -0.4 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 1.32 on a thin 1,641 contracts, ATM IV 120%, event-implied move 14.9%. The tape is -8.8% over 5 sessions and -8.5% over 20, about -12.6% from the CEO's $28.59 RSU tax-withholding price on 2026-09-02. Reaction history: 6 of 7 prior prints fell, four by more than 10%; Q1 FY27 fell about 5% after an EPS beat ($0.17 vs $0.02) and a raised sales guide.

findings.finding: The company has told the market where Q2 EPS should land. On the Q1 call the CFO said 'roughly 20% of our total annual adjusted EPS outlook in the first half of the year, with roughly 15% in the second quarter'. On the maintained $3.25-3.75 FY guide that is $0.49-0.56, midpoint ~$0.525. Consensus is $0.50-0.51, so the street sits at the low-middle of the company's own implied number. Q1 came in at $0.17 against a $0.02 consensus, i.e. the company beat its own cadence in Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-07-08): EPS beat by $0.15 and revenue beat by ~$27m, yet the stock fell about 5%, and the baseline records -10.2% for that event window. Q2 FY26 (2025-10-09): EPS beat ($0.59 vs $0.54) and revenue beat, and the stock fell 25% on the guide. This name has not paid for reported-quarter beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $0.50-0.51 is not above the guide-implied midpoint, so no beat on cadence is in the bar. If the market had priced the company hitting its own cadence, consensus and the whisper would sit at or above $0.525 (the whisper is $0.55, which is consistent with a small expected beat). It lands inside guidance, so it is small.
findings.independence: The bar comes from Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/node/61988956) and Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HELE). Both readings of the cadence come from the same Q1 call transcript.

findings.finding: Revenue consensus is in the upper half of what the H1 guide implies. Management guided H1 sales growth 'in the low to mid single digits' with $4-5m pulled out of Q2 into Q1 by the earlier Prime Day. With Q1 at $402.1m (+8.2%) on a $371.7m + $431.8m prior-year H1, that implies Q2 of roughly $425-450m (-1.5% to +4%). Consensus is $441-443m (+2.2% to +2.6% YoY).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 revenue beat by ~7% and the stock still fell; Q2 FY26 revenue beat ($431.8m vs $418.8m) and the stock fell 25%. A revenue miss here has no clean precedent in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Preview copy quotes the $443m consensus without reconciling it to the H1 cadence net of the Prime Day pull-forward. If it had been reconciled, consensus would sit nearer the guide midpoint of about $437m. It lands inside the guided range, so it is small.
findings.independence: Same transcript as the EPS cadence finding, but a different line (sales rather than EPS), and it points the other way. Q1 sales figures are from the 8-K exhibit 99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000916789/000091678926000094/fy27_q1xex-991.htm). The year-ago $431.8m comes from https://www.benzinga.com/node/61988956.

findings.finding: The FY27 outlook assumed 'tariff rates in place as of June 2026' would hold. On 2026-07-24 Section 122 expired and new Section 301 duties replaced it with no time limit: China, Vietnam and Thailand went to ~12.5% from 10% (+2.5 points), and finished consumer electronics lost their broad exemption. HELE sources its Beauty & Wellness appliances (dryers, fans, thermometers) and much of Home & Outdoor from Asia and targets China below 20% of COGS only by the end of FY27. That is a cost the July guide did not include, most of it landing in H2 COGS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this stock trades on. The -25% (2025-10-09) and -23% (2025-07-10) prints were guidance cuts. The +20.5% (2026-04-23) came with the initial FY27 guide. In Q1 FY27 the EPS guide was held despite cost inflation and the stock fell.
findings.why_not_priced: The rate change is public, but whether HELE absorbs it inside the maintained $3.25-3.75 is not. If it were priced as a cut, the street's FY numbers would sit at the low end of the guide; the Benzinga/EW Q2 consensus sits at the low-middle of the guide-implied range. Small, because management said refunds would be a 'buffer' against inflation above plan.
findings.independence: The guide assumption is in the Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000916789/000091678926000094/fy27_q1xex-991.htm). The CFO said 'cost inflation has outstripped the benefit of tariff refunds' (https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/osprey-brand-owner-says-high-supply-chain-costs-are-outpacing-ieepa-tariff/825081/, 2026-07-15). The company-level transmission is an inference (proxy).

findings.finding: HELE has $71m of IEEPA tariffs paid outside its guide, about $3/share pre-tax on a ~$575m market cap. Only the ~$9.2m Phase I is included in the guide, with the bulk of it collected in Q2. Since the July call: Phase II CAPE opened 2026-06-29 and HELE said it was preparing to file; by early August CBP had sent ~$71bn of refunds to Treasury and importers called the process 'smoother than anticipated'; Target booked a $994m refund in its quarter to 2026-08-01; CBP confirmed Phase 3 (liquidated entries, CIT plaintiffs) for 2026-10-06. Any Phase II collection or a firmer timeline disclosed on 10-08 is upside the guide excludes. Management has said it will reinvest 'the bulk' of refunds and use them as an inflation buffer, so the path to the EPS guide is partial.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 FY27 the $1.8m Phase I recognition and the $71m disclosure came with a held EPS guide, and the stock fell. No print yet has carried a Phase II amount.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock trades at ~7x the midpoint of its own EPS guide and the street's FY27 (Zacks $2.85) sits below the guide, so the market is giving no credit for refunds beyond Phase I. If $71m were priced at even half value, the stock would not sit 17% off its 52-week high into a print with a balanced skew. It is small because management has pre-committed to reinvest most of it.
findings.independence: CBP Phase 2/3 timeline: https://www.thompsonhine.com/insights/cbp-launches-phase-2-of-the-ieepa-tariff-refund-process-and-confirms-development-of-phase-3/ and https://www.internationaltradeinsights.com/2026/09/cbp-states-cape-phase-3-will-deploy-on-october-6-2026/. Refund flow: https://www.hklaw.com/en/news/intheheadlines/2026/08/tariff-refunds-are-flowing-the-real-fight-is-over-who-gets-them (2026-08-03). Target's $994m: https://www.retail-insight-network.com/news/targets-q2-net-earnings-rose-100-8/. All of these are system-level; none is HELE-specific beyond the July disclosure.

findings.finding: Retail and peer read-through for HELE's Jun-Aug quarter is mildly positive. Target's quarter to Aug 1 had comps +3.8% with all six categories up, beauty up high single digits and home improving. Dick's (Hydro Flask's expanded-distribution partner) had DICK'S-business comps +4.9%. YETI's Q2 sales were +9% with drinkware +2% and US drinkware flat. Newell's sales grew for the first time in four years and it raised its guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no precedent for peer read-through in the baseline. Q1 FY27 sales were strong (+8.2%) and the stock fell anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: These are counterparty prints that came after HELE last spoke on 2026-07-08, and the street's Q2 revenue sits only ~2.5% above the year-ago quarter. If the read-through were in the bar, revenue consensus would sit above the guide-implied midpoint. This is a proxy; retailers were described as 'cautious' with 'elevated promotional intensity' on HELE's own call.
findings.independence: Dick's: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/4018592/dick-s-sporting-goods-inc-reports-second-quarter-results. YETI: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001670592/000167059226000039/yeti-20260813xex991pressre.htm. Newell: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260731380569/en/. Each is a different company with a different quarter end, and all are proxies.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is short-heavy and de-risked. 12.77% of float is short at 9.0 days to cover (2026-09-15), and the stock is -8.8% in 5 sessions to $24.99, down from $28.59 on 2026-09-02. Street full-year numbers sit below the company guide (Zacks FY27 $2.85 vs guide $3.25-3.75), so a held or raised guide meets a market that is not long it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Against it: 6 of 7 prints fell, including on beats. For it: the one up print (+20.5%, 2026-04-23) came when a guide landed above a sceptical street.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest and the run-in are public, and the option market prices a balanced 14.9% move with no skew. That balance itself shows the squeeze is not being paid for. The drawdown has no identified cause in this search, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The CEO's Form 4 at $28.59 on 2026-09-02 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/916789/000091678926000123/0000916789-26-000123-index.htm) dates the price level. Zacks FY27 $2.85: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/q2-eps-estimates-for-helen-of-troy-raised-by-zacks-research-2026-07-31/.

outside_window.finding: Phase III/IV IEEPA refund claims, which the CFO said may extend into fiscal 2028, are not collectable inside this window whatever is said on the call. They are worth nothing to this trade beyond the commentary.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly positive and agree with the crowded short and the run-in. They cut against the name's reaction history (6 of 7 prints down, beats sold), and the balanced -0.4 skew gives no help either way.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6: EPS cadence finding lands inside company guidance; 0.5 -> 0.3. Bar confirmed by two agreeing sources plus guide, so no cap.
Lessons 5 and 7: the Section 301 tariff finding is macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by HELE and sits against a crowded short; -1.0 -> -0.6.
Lesson 2: the IEEPA refund upside is a one_off whose path to the guide is partial because management pre-committed to reinvest the bulk; 1.0 -> 0.6.
Lesson 5: retail read-through is a proxy; 0.5 -> 0.3.
Lessons 1 and 5: positioning and the unexplained drawdown sized down 1.0 -> 0.5; the name sells its beats, so p_up 52 -> 51.
Lesson 8: abs_move_pct raised 14 -> 15 against systematic understatement (implied 14.9, median reaction 12.0).
